title: Diabetic foot screen: press a 10 g monofilament perpendicular until it bends at four sole sites, testing beside a callus
instruction: Screen the training manikin's foot with the monofilament: press it perpendicular to the sole until it bends, about 1.5 s, at the big toe and 1st, 3rd and 5th metatarsal heads, beside any callus; then put the pen back.
context: Preventive health. About 38 million Americans have diabetes (CDC). Up to a third get a foot ulcer (NIDDK); diabetes caused about 130,000 amputation hospital stays in 2016, and CDC estimates regular foot exams and education could prevent up to 85% of these amputations. The ADA and IWGDF screen for lost protective sensation at least yearly with a 10 g monofilament on the plantar hallux and 1st, 3rd and 5th metatarsal heads: perpendicular, pressed until it bends, about 2 s, never slid, never on callus (test at its edge). An angled, jabbed, slid or on-callus touch gives a false result. The sole is curved, so each site needs its own approach line and a stop inside the filament's 11 mm bend window.
setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench), arm bases at y +-30.5. Foot: a rigid life-size adult right foot model (Anatomical Chart Company class), skin sRGB (224, 172, 145), 26.1 cm heel to toe, 9.7 cm across the ball, with a rounded heel, a raised medial arch, a pad over each metatarsal head on a transverse curve, and five toes with pulps (a smooth mesh, foot_mesh.npz). Its ankle cut is bolted to a dark (45, 47, 50) sloped board on a column and base plate, 3 kg in all, loose on the bench: the sole faces the robots, tipped back 30 deg from vertical and turned 30 deg toward the robots' left; the seed shifts the stand -1.2 to +1.2 cm along y. Test sites on the curved skin (point; outward skin normal as x, y, z) with the stand unshifted: plantar hallux (48.1, -7.0, 25.4; -0.56, 0.23, 0.80), 1st metatarsal head (45.7, -6.2, 20.7; -0.86, 0.00, 0.51), 3rd (46.9, -2.9, 21.1; -0.72, 0.43, 0.54), 5th (48.6, 0.4, 19.4; -0.41, 0.71, 0.57); the normals differ by 21 to 50 deg, and the skin curves away from each site (the normal 14 mm away differs by 13 to 29 deg). One seeded site carries a yellow (226, 196, 84) callus, a patch 18 mm across and 1.5 mm proud that follows the skin, centred on the site. Pen: Owen Mumford Neuropen, blue (30, 90, 190) barrel 16 mm across and 14.0 cm long, 15 g, white nose 6 mm long; a white 10 g (5.07) nylon monofilament 38 mm long comes out of the nose along the axis (it buckles at about 0.1 N, 10 g); it has a slight set, curving toward a white stripe printed along the barrel, its tip 2.9 mm off the barrel's axis. It lies loose across two grey (120, 124, 128) cradle posts 11.6 cm apart (slots 19 mm wide, barrel axis 4.5 cm up) at x 28, centred on y -16 (the seed shifts the pen -0.6 to +0.6 cm along the cradle), filament end toward +y, stripe facing the robots.
scoring: Score 0 if at any point the filament touches the callus, the pen's barrel touches the foot, the pen falls off the bench, or the foot model moves more than 20 mm. Otherwise 0.25 for each site whose first contact was a correct test (a touch belongs to the nearest site within 18 mm): the filament tip landed within 8 mm of the site (on the callus site: 2 to 8 mm outside the callus edge), the barrel tip came within 35 mm of the skin (the filament bent) but never closer than 24 mm, the pen's axis stayed within 15 deg of the skin normal at the landing point and the tip within 3 mm of its landing point while bent, and the contact lasted 1.0 to 3.0 s. A site's later contacts never count. Four sites score 0.75 until the pen lies back in its cradle with no gripper centre within 5 cm of it: then 1.0 (success, held 1 s). Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Lay the pen back across its cradle posts, filament toward the robots' left, its centre within 6 mm of the cradle's centre (the seed sets the offset). Put the foot stand back with the 3rd metatarsal head at x 46.9, its y between -4.1 and -1.7 (seeded), and move the callus to the seeded site. Real trial: stick the moleskin callus on the seeded site, re-ink the site rings and replace the monofilament after 70 to 90 uses (IWGDF).
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz. Foot: rigid smooth triangle-mesh skin (arch, metatarsal pads, toes) colliding through convex tiles within 0.5 mm of it; real trial uses a $99 rigid foot model. Filament: 4 rigid capsule links on sprung hinges (1.0e-3 N m/rad, buckling load 0.098 N), bending in one plane, collided 1.6 mm thick (real 0.4 mm), 0.1 g links for solver stability. Callus is painted (no collider). Touches, angles and slide are scored from geometry against the skin mesh. Masses are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps, seed 0); scripted demo: 1.0 (seeds 0-7, success at steps 1104-1157); do nothing, random joints, random reaches, naive straight-ahead press: 0.0; press along the sole's mean normal: 0.25 (only the 3rd metatarsal head, where that normal is right)
